newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on KEPCO decline.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on KEPCO decline.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply lower on Friday as heavily-index weighted KEPCO and Samsung Electronics tumbled, and brokers said the consolidation would continue next week.
The composite stock index shed 12.38 points or 1.55 percent to provisionally close at 785.19.

"Sharp falls in KEPCO and Samsung Electronics triggered much of the index's fall today," said Park Ki-pyong of Hanyang Securities. "Investors are now questioning how much new money will really flow into the market after the foreign stock ownership ceiling is raised next month."
Electricity monopoly KEPCO shed 1,100 won to 26,700 as domestic investors grew nervous over a slowdown in foreign buying on the unofficial over-the-counter market.
Still gloomy prospects of an upturn in the semiconductor industry dragged Samsaung Electronics down 2,300 won to 57,200.
Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities said rising tensions between Iraq and the United States also caused selling in large-cap manufacturing shares.
"Investors are worried the tension will lead to rising oil prices and a stronger dollar, which will badly affect our exports and inflation," Kim said.
